subject: Hosting & migration follow-up — Acme.ai deployment options and next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Morales <sylvia@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting & migration follow-up — Acme.ai deployment options and next steps

Hi Sylvia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align on the migration path: 

Recap from our discussion:
- Current state: self-hosted LLM endpoints on legacy GPU clusters (NVIDIA V100), mixed traffic (API for end-user features + internal batch jobs).
- Primary goals: reduce ops overhead, lower per-token costs, and meet compliance needs for customer data.
- Constraints: cannot send certain training artifacts off-prem without additional controls; SOC2/compliance is a hard requirement.

Clarifying questions (so we size the right option):
1) Baseline throughput: what’s your sustained qps and peak qps during business hours? (you mentioned spikes)
2) Retention & logs: how long do you need request/response logs retained for audit?
3) Data residency & model artifacts: do you plan to migrate your fine-tuned model weights, or do you prefer us to host a compatible model variant?
4) Timeline: target migration/PoC start date?

From our side, three realistic paths we can take (short notes):
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, but requires sending inference traffic to our hosted endpoints — usually not suitable when fine-tuned weights or strict data residency is required.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool): Dedicated GPUs in a customer-dedicated VPC with isolation and predictable throughput — good mid-path if you want lower ops work with network isolation (VPC peering).
- Private deployment (VPC private control plane or on-prem): Full control plane inside your VPC or fully on-prem for air-gapped needs — best for strict compliance but longer to provision.

Suggested next step: propose a 2-week PoC on Dedicated capacity (dedicated VPC) to validate latency/cost while we parallelize the compliance review for Private. PoC scope: 2 GPUs, mimic peak traffic, run perf tests + a short eval suite. If the compliance team signs off, we can pivot the same config into a Private deployment.

I attached a short PoC scope doc and a preliminary checklist. If you prefer, we can send an NDA + SOW draft before PoC. 

Proposed timeslots for kickoff: Apr 26–28 or May 3–5 (30–60 minute kickoff + tech runbook review). Which works best for you?

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172

From: Sylvia Morales <sylvia@acme.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake@acme.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting & migration follow-up — Acme.ai deployment options and next steps

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and constraints from our side: 

- Throughput: sustained ~800 QPM across our production region, peaks up to ~6k QPM during campaign runs (roughly 9–11am PST).
- Retention: we need request/response logs retained for 90 days for audit (PII redaction possible).
- Models/artifacts: our fine-tuned Llama-based models include proprietary prompt templates and tokenizers. We are uncomfortable transferring raw model weights to a third party without additional controls (encryption + KMS in our cloud).
- Network: we require VPC peering or private link for production traffic; public-hosted API is acceptable for a short sandbox but not for production.
- Timeline: target PoC late next week (Apr 26–30) if feasible.

We attached our security requirements spreadsheet (security_requirements.xlsx).

Given the constraints, Dedicated capacity in a customer-managed VPC is likely our preferred initial approach, with the possibility of moving to a Private deployment later. Can you confirm how Dedicated handles customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) and whether we can keep model weights in our S3 bucket (you would pull into the Dedicated nodes via VPC). Also, do you support prefix/KV caching for reduced token cost?

Thanks — Sylvia

--
Sylvia Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme.ai
Sylvia.Morales@acme.ai | +1 212-555-0147

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Morales <sylvia@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting & migration follow-up — Acme.ai deployment options and next steps

Sylvia — great, thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Quick answers inline and next steps: 

- KMS/BYOK & weights: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and can be configured to pull weights/artifacts from your S3 via a private VPC endpoint. For Private on-prem we can support an air-gapped transfer process.
- Caching: yes — runtime supports prefix and KV caching; we can enable a cache layer in the Dedicated cluster to reduce per-token compute for repeated prefixes. We'll include cache configs in the PoC scope.
- Retention: can configure retention to 90 days and redact PII at the proxy layer before logging; we'll capture that in the runbook.

Proposed approach (concise):
1) Start PoC on Dedicated capacity inside your customer VPC (2 GPU nodes to simulate peak).
2) Run our perf + correctness suite against a representative prompt set (we'll need a sanitized subset from you).
3) Parallel compliance track: our security team will review the spreadsheet and provide SOC2 artifacts; if needed, we move to Private deployment.

I've attached the proposed PoC scope (proposed-poc-scope.md) and a short checklist. I'll loop Ben to help with technical onboarding and Karthik to estimate cost and capacity. Can you confirm which day between Apr 26–28 you'd like to kick off? Also, please share a sanitized prompt set and the account in HubSpot if you want the PoC to be tracked there.

Thanks — Neha

--

Subject: Re: Hosting & migration follow-up — Acme.ai deployment options and next steps

Neha — Apr 27 works best for us for a kickoff (30–45 min). We can provide a sanitized prompt set by EOD Apr 23. 

A few asks before kickoff:
- Please send an estimated cost for a 2-week Dedicated PoC (2xG40-equivalent nodes) so I can get internal pre-approval.
- Please share your SOC2 folder or a link to the report so our security team can scan immediately.
- We'll need a short onboarding doc for the VPC peering steps (security will want the network diagram).

If you can get these by Apr 23, we'll be set to start Apr 27. Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Sylvia
